title: After the big wave
hook: A big wave passes and immunity slowly fades. Where does the town end up?

knows: the SIR picture: susceptible, sick, recovered
an epidemic peaks when the susceptible share falls to 1/R0
doesNotKnow: that when immunity fades, the infection settles into recurring, shrinking waves around an endemic level
that the susceptible share settles at 1/R0

misconception: After a big wave the disease is gone for good.
objective: The learner can explain that fading immunity refills the susceptible pool, so waves return, and that the infection holds the susceptible share at 1/R0 (half when R0 = 2) whatever the immunity length.

claims.text: In the SIRS model the endemic equilibrium has susceptible share S* = 1/R0; with R0 = 2 that is 50%.
claims.source: Anderson R.M. & May R.M. (1991) Infectious Diseases of Humans, Oxford UP, ch. 6; Keeling M.J. & Rohani P. (2008) Modeling Infectious Diseases in Humans and Animals, Princeton UP, ch. 2. dI/dt = 0 with I > 0 requires beta S = gamma.

claims.text: On the stage (infection 0.4/day, recovery 0.2/day, immunity fading at 1/100 per day, 0.1% sick on day 0), waves peak on days 34, 185, 329, 473, 617 and 761 with 50.7%, 50.2% and then about 50.0% susceptible at the daily snapshot (shares within 0.05 points of half are printed to two decimals); by day 900 the town is at 50.00% susceptible and 2.4% sick.
claims.source: Euler step 0.01 day, deterministic, no seed; peaks are local maxima of the daily sick share (artifacts/scratch/w3life/sirs.mjs and revision 2026-10-13 rerun): peak S 50.7, 50.2, 50.0, 50.0, 50.0, 50.0%; day 900 S 50.0%, I 2.4%. Parameters are the brief's, made up. | v3 (2026-10-14): reveal derives 1/R0, quotes only the wave and day the learner reached (settled now needs day 900); locked stage hides the half line; previous verification void, needs re-check. | REVISED v4 2026-10-14 (demo-builder, wave D r5): Only the display precision changed: susceptible shares within 0.05 points of half now show two decimals (pctS), so 'over half' / 'under half' in the new trend text can be read off the number. Builder re-run: S(900) = 0.50001, I(900) = 0.0238. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 22): Own re-implementation of simulate(100): peaks on days 34, 185, 329, 473, 617, 761; pctS prints 50.7%, 50.2%, 50.00%, 50.00%, 50.00%, 50.00%; day 900 S = 0.500012 (50.00%), I = 2.4%. 0.05-point two-decimal rule matches pctS (|x - 0.5| < 0.0005).

claims.text: The wave peaks when the susceptible share is about 1/R0, half the town when R0 = 2: with R0 = 2 each sick person infects 2 others only if everyone can catch it, so at half each infects 1 and cases hold steady; above half they grow, below half they shrink while fading immunity refills the susceptibles.
claims.source: dI/dt = (beta S - gamma) I changes sign at S = gamma/beta = 1/R0. | v3 (2026-10-14): reveal derives 1/R0, quotes only the wave and day the learner reached (settled now needs day 900); locked stage hides the half line; previous verification void, needs re-check.

claims.text: The immunity length changes how many are sick at the endemic level and how far apart the waves are, not the roughly 50% susceptible share: with immunity of about 50 days, 4.5% are sick at day 900; with about 200 days, 1.3% (50% and 49.8% susceptible).
claims.source: artifacts/scratch/w3life/sirs.mjs: L = 50 gives S 50.00%, I 4.55% at day 900, waves about 104 days apart; L = 200 gives S 49.77% (still oscillating, 48.9-50.7% over days 700-900), I 1.29%, waves about 200 days apart.

claims.text: The model is a made-up infection with random mixing and no births, deaths, seasons or vaccines; 'about 100 days' is an average (immunity fades at a constant rate).
claims.source: Model choice in Demo.tsx; stated in the question, on the stage ('Toy: R0 2, immunity fades after about 100 days') and in the reveal.

claims.text: R0 = 2 means each sick person infects 2 others when everyone can catch the infection; 'susceptible' means able to catch it; recovered people are immune until immunity fades.
claims.source: Standard definitions (Keeling & Rohani 2008 ch. 2); model parameters beta = 0.4, gamma = 0.2 give R0 = beta/gamma = 2.

claims.text: Stage readout on non-peak days: 'cases growing: over half can catch it', 'cases shrinking: under half can catch it', or 'cases holding steady: half can catch it' (within 0.01 points of half).
claims.source: In the SIR(S) model dI/dt = I(βS − γ), so with β = 0.4 and γ = 0.2 cases grow exactly when S > γ/β = 1/R0 = 0.5. trend() in Demo.tsx tests the stage's own S. Replaces the old 'cases growing/shrinking' label, which compared daily snapshots and read as noise at day 890 (r5). | REVISED v4 2026-10-14 (demo-builder, wave D r5): new sentence. New stage text: shows the grow/shrink cause (above or below half) on stage. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 22): trend() threshold |S - 0.5| < 0.0001 = 0.01 points. Own node over every slider day (step 5): 0 cases where the grow/shrink text disagrees with the sign of beta S - gamma; no day shows 50.00% with grow/shrink text. Note: days 880-885 print '50.01% susceptible, ... cases holding steady' (inside the stated 0.01-point band).

recall.question: A made-up infection with R0 = 4 gives immunity that slowly fades. After the waves settle in a simple well-mixed model, roughly what share of people are susceptible?
recall.why: The infection holds the susceptible share at 1/R0 = 1/4: more and cases grow and drain it, fewer and cases shrink while fading immunity refills it.
